questions.title: Role of the Base Case
questions.description: What does the base case of a recursive function do?
questions.Option1: It makes the next recursive call
questions.Option3: It stops the recursion by returning without recursing further
questions.Option4: It doubles the input for the next call

questions.title: Call Stack Frames
questions.description: What happens on the call stack when a function calls itself?
questions.Option1: All recursive calls share one single set of variables
questions.Option2: Each call gets its own frame holding its own parameters and local variables
questions.Option3: Python stores the pending calls in a queue instead of a stack
questions.Option4: The new call replaces the caller's frame immediately

questions.title: Recursion Limit
questions.description: What does Python do when recursion goes too deep?
questions.Option1: It silently returns None from the deepest call
questions.Option2: It raises RecursionError once the stack exceeds the recursion limit (about 1000 frames)
questions.Option3: It reboots the interpreter and restarts the function
questions.Option4: It automatically converts the recursion into a loop

questions.title: Subset Generation Doubling
questions.description: When generating all subsets by iterating over the elements, how does the collection grow?
questions.Option1: Each element adds exactly one new subset
questions.Option3: The count stays constant until the last element
questions.Option4: Every existing subset spawns a copy that also includes the new element, doubling the count
